angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 476,346 km at 112.42 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.8954 +/- 0.0157 mas (same row, RUWE 1.21): 112.42 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.6847 +/- 0.0613 solar radii from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-3082 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract): 476,346 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.664 +/- 0.0798 solar masses from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-3082 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4263 +/- 100 K from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3082 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3082 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-3082.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.589, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
